outcomes.original: Filing step: Register the business entity with the California Secretary of State (LLC or corporation) and obtain a federal Employer Identification Number (EIN) from the IRS. What to say: File Articles of Organization (LLC, $70) or Articles of Incorporation (corporation, $100–$150) online at bizfile.sos.ca.gov; file the Statement of Information within 90 days ($20 LLC, $25 corporation). Apply for the EIN at irs.gov/businesses immediately after forming the entity; it is issued the same day and is needed for the bank account, business registration, seller's permit, and all city permits. If operating as a sole proprietor, skip the SOS filing and file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the SF County Clerk instead, but the EIN is still required.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Register for a California Seller's Permit with CDTFA and for payroll tax withholding with the California Employment Development Department (EDD). What to say: Register online at onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov for the seller's permit (free, often issued same day; required for selling prepared food). Both registrations require the EIN.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Obtain a San Francisco Business Registration Certificate from the Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector. What to say: Register online at sftreasurer.org/business; the fee is tiered by gross receipts (e.g., $55 up to $100k, $95 up to $250k for 2026–27, each plus a $4 state fee). The Business Account Number (BAN) is issued within 1–5 days and is required for every other city permit (health, building, Planning, sign). Renew by the last day of February each year. If the public-facing name differs from the legal entity name, file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the County Clerk and publish it in a newspaper once a week for four weeks.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Submit a health plan check application to SF Department of Public Health for the new or remodeled kitchen, finishes, equipment and menu, with scaled drawings, photos, and a three-compartment sink and hand-wash sink layout. What to say: Apply online through the DPH portal with the BAN, Location ID (LIN) and EIN. The fee is $828 (small remodel, 3 hrs), $1,241 (bar/prepackaged, 4.5 hrs), or $2,207 (new restaurant, 8 hrs) for FY 2026–27, with extra review at $276/hr. Submit two sets of scaled drawings showing all equipment, sinks, walls, doors, and menu describing preparation steps. Make sure 'health' is a routing station on any building permit application filed at the same time. Schedule a pre-final inspection at ~80% complete and a final inspection at least two weeks ahead with your plan reviewer; both inspections must pass before the permit to operate is issued.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File a building permit application with SF Department of Building Inspection for tenant improvements (kitchen build-out, finishes, ADA upgrades, storefront work), with plans stamped by an architect if the work is not minor. What to say: The building permit application must list 'Planning' as a routing station per Planning Code Section 175(a) (in force since October 6, 2025). If a CUA is required (see step 1), the CUA must be approved before DBI will issue the building permit. Include plumbing, mechanical and electrical plans; licensed subcontractors will pull separate permits for those trades. Fees are a percentage of construction valuation (typically $800–$15,000 for restaurant tenant improvements). Request expedited review if eligible. Building permit review takes 14–120 days depending on plan completeness and whether the project needs Planning or fire review.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Complete tenant improvements and obtain final inspections from DBI, SFPUC (grease interceptor), and SF Fire Department (if occupant load is 50 or more), then schedule the final health inspection with DPH. What to say: Call for a final building inspection when the space is complete and matches the approved plans. SFPUC will inspect and approve the grease interceptor as part of the FOG program; submit the Installation Verification Form to earn a 14.2% sewer bill reduction. If the occupant load is 50 or more, obtain a Place of Assembly permit from the Fire Department ($446 at 49 South Van Ness) and schedule a fire inspection before the health inspection. Schedule the final health inspection at least two weeks in advance; the inspector will confirm the facility matches approved plans, all sinks and equipment are in place, hot water is available, and a certified food safety manager is on staff. The permit to operate is issued after the inspection passes.
